target_zone_range.evidence_basis: South-central Texas floristic voucher set explicitly records G. bipinnatifida in Uvalde, Medina, and Real counties; Williamson and Travis are also independently documented.
target_zone_range.guardrail: Exact county vouchers used; no broad ecoregion inference.

morphology.look_here_first: Start with the leaves. Prairie verbena has larger, strongly dissected leaves that are often twice pinnately cut, giving a distinctly feathery outline. The plant is usually more spreading and coarser than low verbena, with rounded purple flower clusters on longer shoots.
diagnostic_traits: leaves deeply 1–2-pinnately dissected, often strongly feathery
spreading hairs with some glandular hairs
commonly 10–40 cm tall in Williamson material

confusers.separator: G. pumila is lower and more compact, with smaller broadly ovate leaves divided into fewer broader lobes and a very short dense spike that does not elongate much in fruit. G. bipinnatifida looks more finely cut and feathery.
